pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Do not force sanitization when constructing inventory. This fixes a regression introduced in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/60912 which breaks 'force_valid_group_names'.

Fixes #68851

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
constructed

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Before:
```
ansible-inventory -i inventory/internal_services/inventory.gcp.yml --graph
[WARNING]: Invalid characters were found in group names and automatically replaced, use -vvvv to see details
@all:
  |--@bastion:
  |  |--just-passing-through
  |--@etcd:
  |  |--etcd-1
  |--@kube_master:
  |  |--master-1
  |--@kube_node:
  |  |--node-1
  |--@ungrouped:
```

After:
```
ansible-inventory -i inventory/internal_services/inventory.gcp.yml --graph
[WARNING]: Invalid characters were found in group names but not replaced, use -vvvv to see details
@all:
  |--@bastion:
  |  |--just-passing-through
  |--@etcd:
  |  |--etcd-1
  |--@kube-master:
  |  |--master-1
  |--@kube-node:
  |  |--node-1
  |--@ungrouped:
```

Hello, @bcoca
It looks like a lot of engineers are waiting for this request to be merged.
Can you merge it, please?

The base constructed methods were intended to always ensure valid group names. A change like this would affect all plugins using the constructed features, rather than only the ones overriding the sanitization. `force_valid_group_names` is a global toggle for the core engine sanitization, which occurs after plugins have sanitized/not sanitized groups. `_add_host_to_composed_groups` has been fixed in #73429 so plugins authors can override the sanitization function. I'm also adding some documentation for that here https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/73497.

issue_context.title: force_valid_group_names "ignore" has no effect on Ansible 2.9
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
Setting `force_valid_group_names = ignore` or `ANSIBLE_TRANSFORM_INVALID_GROUP_CHARS=ignore` should be enough to get Ansible to not mangle group names, but in Ansible 2.9 it appears to have no effect, rendering that version of Ansible unusable. Reverting to 2.7.11 "resolves" the issue.

I tried:
`export ANSIBLE_TRANSFORM_INVALID_GROUP_CHARS=ignore`
`export TRANSFORM_INVALID_GROUP_CHARS=ignore`
Setting `force_valid_group_names=ignore` in [defaults] of ansible.cfg (see https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray/blob/master/ansible.cfg#L7-L8)

I banged my head against this for a few hours thinking my ansible.cfg wasn't being read properly, etc. Downgrading Ansible finally moved me forward.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
Core?

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
NOT WORKING:
```
 config file = /home/erulabs/.ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/erulabs/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /home/erulabs/.local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible-playbook
  python version = 3.7.5 (default, Nov 20 2019, 09:21:52) [GCC 9.2.1 20191008]
```
Working properly:
```
% ansible --version
ansible 2.7.11
  config file = /home/erulabs/.ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = [u'/home/erulabs/.ansible/plugins/modules', u'/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /home/erulabs/.local/lib/python2.7/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /home/erulabs/.local/bin//ansible
  python version = 2.7.17 (default, Nov  7 2019, 10:07:09) [GCC 9.2.1 20191008]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
`ansible-config dump --only-changed` has no output. No configuration was changed between 2.7 and 2.9.

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
Both versions tested on Ubuntu 19.10


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
Try to use almost any Ansible playbook or role (kubespray for example), and notice everything is highly broken due to lack of force_valid_group_names taking effect.  (see https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray/blob/master/ansible.cfg#L7-L8)

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
Groups are properly populated

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
No hosts match groups with invalid characters in them

This could be, if an inventory plugin chooses to use the 'to_safe_group_name' function in  [`lib/ansible/plugin/inventory/__init__.py`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py#L45), which forces sanitization. This is currently up to the plugin author/maintainers. Inventory plugins using the '_sanitize_group_name' method may be using that indirectly, by default.
**However**, it looks like the repo you pointed to uses an ini inventory, and the ini inventory plugin doesn't force sanitization (and also doesn't sanitize by default, for backwards compatibility).

>  ... and notice everything is highly broken ...

Please provide the actual output from a small, simple reproducer (for example, an inventory file and which plugin should be used to parse it). There isn't enough information to reproduce. You can use `ansible-inventory -i inventory_file --graph` to see what the group names are.

> ansible-config dump --only-changed has no output.

It should, if you have correctly set the configuration for the group names toggle to ignore before running the command. Use that command to help make sure you're setting the toggle correctly.

Here is an example, note it requires Hetzner Cloud servers and a token:

```
plugin: hcloud
token: some_token
network: kubernetes
keyed_groups:
  - key: labels
    prefix: ""
    separator: ""
```

In the above example the labels have invalid characters i.e. 'kube-master'. The plugin follows the path below:

1. The hcloud inventory plugin for querying Hetzner Cloud uses the Constructable base class
2. The plugin calls self._add_hosts_to_keyed_groups
3. That calls self._sanitize_group_name
4. This hits the line below which sets force=True when calling to_safe_group_name on inventory/group.py

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/bbdf77a59f50306b34161efc148b572ab257a537/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py#L45

This makes it impossible to override using TRANSFORM_INVALID_GROUP_CHARS.

@verokarhu this is not a regression, the 'constructed' functions were always meant to default to warn. Plugin authors have the ability to override or not use these functions.

@jrmcdonald At this point i think the issue lies with fixing the plugin itself and not the default function.

> @verokarhu this is not a regression, the 'constructed' functions were always meant to default to warn. Plugin authors have the ability to override or not use these functions.

This change doesn't remove the warning, the regression comes from the previous change enabling force which [completely bypasses the configuration flag.](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/inventory/group.py#L40) Are you saying that this should be fixed in `group.py` instead, i.e. by ignoring the force flag?

@bcoca Thanks for looking at this, however based on the example I provided I'm not sure what else a plugin would be expected to do when calling `_add_host_to_composed_groups` and using constructed as a base? the constructed functions are meant to do this by default, it is up to the caller to override that behaviour by supplying their own validation.  

The toggle is supposed to affect the 'global' verification, not per plugin ones. Plugins are free to deviate.

@bcoca Thanks for that explanation, I understand the rationale there. I think that @verokarhu has identified the issue, even if their proposed fix is not in line with the rationale that you explained. The change they linked to, [#60912](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/60912), changes the call on line 375 of `__init__.py` from:

If it was still using `self._sanitize_group_name` then I could override that easily.

review_comments:
Plugins should be able to override sanitization by setting self._sanitize_group_name, but otherwise the constructed features always sanitize.

This would keep the warning for the change in behavior in 2.8 while letting plugins override:
```diff
diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py
index d34c1e0a0f..9281605298 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py
@@ -377,7 +377,13 @@ class Constructable(object):
             self.templar.available_variables = variables
             for group_name in groups:
                 conditional = "{%% if %s %%} True {%% else %%} False {%% endif %%}" % groups[group_name]
-                group_name = original_safe(group_name, force=True)
+                if self._sanitize_group_name == to_safe_group_name:
+                    # only began to be sanitized in 2.8 - do the same thing as to_safe_group_name but not silently
+                    group_name = original_safe(group_name, force=True)
+                else:
+                    # Allow plugins to do their own sanitization
+                    group_name = self._sanitize_group_name(group_name)
```
On the other hand, maybe the warning isn't needed (there was some confusion because `keyed_groups` sanitized the group names for 2 releases before `groups` began sanitizing) in which case this should be
`group_name = self._sanitize_group_name(group_name)`.

Tested your suggested change snippet. It still mangles group names when `ANSIBLE_TRANSFORM_INVALID_GROUP_CHARS=never` is set in environment.

The PR does the fix the bug as-is though.
I see the problem, the PR as-is disables the mangling completely. So it does the other opposite of not respecting the `TRANSFORM_INVALID_GROUP_CHARS` configuration.

@logan2211  you are incorreclty assuming that this is a toggle for each plugin's validation, it is not, it is for the global validation. Each inventory plugin is free to add it's own validation on top, most do and it is not controlled by that toggle.

This PR alters the behaviour of the plugin which was always meant to filter the invalid names, the plugin itself never allowed - in group names.

> the plugin itself never allowed - in group names.

That's not true. Every release prior to 2.8 allowed "-" in group names using the `constructed` plugin, hence #70741. That's why I'm here -- my inventory went from functioning normally, to completely broken when upgrading from 2.7 -> 2.8 due to the group names being arbitrarily mangled by the new behavior.

After reading the docs I thought I found a configuration that allowed disabling this unnecessary mangling behavior, but after finding that it does not restore previous functionality, I ended up opening #70741.

> Each inventory plugin is free to add it's own validation on top, most do and it is not controlled by that toggle.

`constructed` did not mangle group names shown in the #70741 example prior to the change in 2.8 that added the global system. I'd think that the global implementation created a great opportunity for plugins to behave consistently according to a single configuration setting. 

As you said:
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/52748#issuecomment-468017671: "I'm just trying to get the 'general toggle' working with the system w/o breaking any current playbooks"

I'm here because my playbooks are broken. How can we get this fixed?

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/53458#issuecomment-471528717 sums it up very well:
> It is very frustrating to ask for Ansible to not sanitize group names (the current behavior for most things in the current 2.7 version, ec2 is just one case) and have it still replace anything.

@logan2211 There are a lot of plugins which also use this code, hence the 'general toggle'. This would support a fix for `constructed` though - the code in `lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/constructed.py` just needs a way to set `self._sanitize_group_name`.

That could be as simple as adding the import `from ansible.inventory.group import to_safe_group_name` and then in parse() add  `self._sanitize_group_name = to_safe_group_name`.

> There are a lot of plugins which also use this code, hence the 'general toggle'.

I see that. It looks like it would be fairly easy for most of the plugins to use, rather than ignore the configuration parameter that was added. Simply stop using `force=True` in places like: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/__init__.py#L43-L45 so the configuration parameter can work as intended.

> This would support a fix for constructed though - the code in lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/constructed.py just needs a way to set self._sanitize_group_name.
> That could be as simple as adding the import from ansible.inventory.group import to_safe_group_name and then in parse() add self._sanitize_group_name = to_safe_group_name.

Thanks, I adjusted #70765 to match your suggested implementation and confirmed that `constructed` now follows the configuration.

Also note that implementing your suggestion essentially requires a revert of #60912 because calling `original_safe` directly bypasses `self._sanitize_group_name`, so you'll see this reflected in my PR.
